issues.description: is-prime-ideal? has O(R^2 * I) complexity because it performs a nested loop over all ring elements and calls 'member' (a linear search) on the ideal elements inside the inner loop. For a ring of size 1,000, this could result in up to 1 billion operations.
issues.suggested_fix: Convert i-elems to a hash set for O(1) lookups. Also, optimize the logic: the condition is only non-trivial when neither a nor b is in the ideal, so you can iterate over (R \ I) x (R \ I) and verify that a*b is also not in I.

issues.description: ideal-sum and ideal-product generate a cross-product list of size |I1|*|I2| and then call remove-duplicates on it. Since remove-duplicates is O(N^2), the total complexity is O((|I1|*|I2|)^2), which is quartic relative to the size of the ideals.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a hash table or similar structure to collect unique elements during the generation process instead of building an intermediate list and performing an O(N^2) duplicate removal at the end.

issues.description: is-valid-ideal? uses nested loops with linear member checks to verify closure. This results in O(I^3) for additive closure and O(R * I^2) for multiplicative closure, which is inefficient for large rings or ideals.
issues.suggested_fix: Convert i-elems to a hash set to reduce 'member' calls to O(1) time complexity.

issues.description: is-valid-ring-homomorphism? recomputes phi(a) and phi(b) O(R^2) times within the nested loops. If the homomorphism function phi is expensive, this will significantly degrade performance.
issues.code_snippet: (ring-add s (phi a) (phi b)) ... (ring-mul s (phi a) (phi b))
issues.suggested_fix: Lift the computation of (phi a) to the outer loop and (phi b) to the inner loop, or precompute all phi(x) values for the ring elements once.

issues.description: ring-units computes is-unit? for every element, and is-unit? performs a linear scan of all elements. This results in O(R^2) complexity for identifying all units in the ring.
issues.suggested_fix: While O(R^2) is standard for generic finite rings, consider allowing specialized algorithms for specific ring types (e.g., using the extended Euclidean algorithm for Z_n).

summary: Found 5 performance issues: 2 high severity (quartic complexity in ideal operations, cubic complexity in primality check), 2 medium severity (inefficient validation and homomorphism verification), and 1 low severity (quadratic complexity in unit finding).
